findings.text: blocking: `negative_control_log: NEG_LOG_PATH` is a literal placeholder, not a path a reader can open, so the red-control evidence cannot be admitted. The `tests.negative_control` block at manifest.md:34 also claims revision 055d84935, but no complete red log covers that revision: the two runs at 055d84935 (logs/gate-negative-control-130430.log and -130839.log) are truncated after the header and one 'F' with no EXIT= line, while the only complete red control (logs/gate-negative-control-125727.log, exit 1, 2 failed 2 passed) ran at 4ffbc6adf. The pointer must name a readable red log at a revision whose run actually completed.

follow-on: this assertion compares the re-read axis against `record.axis_r`/`record.axis_z`, which export_records.py:243-244 stored from that very reading (`replace(provisional, axis_r=float(axis[0]), axis_z=float(axis[1]))`), so the two sides move together and reverting the read leaves the assertion true; it is not independent of the value under test.

follow-on: `abs(boundary - record.fed_back_psi) <= STORED_TOLERANCE` compares the re-read boundary level against `record.fed_back_psi`, which export_records.py:247 stored from the same read's `boundary_flux`, so both sides derive from the value under test and the assertion cannot redden on a read regression.

follow-on: runtime producer code imports the private helper `_analytic_inputs` from the test module `tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py`, coupling the export to a test file the brief fenced off; the analytic-input source belongs to a support owner rather than a test module.

follow-on: `topology.TopologyConvention.from_cocos(COCOS, float(record.polarity))` duplicates the existing owner `scripts/prototypes/efit_field_swap/orientation.py:48 read_convention(polarity=...)`, which does the same derivation plus its own polarity validation, so the module re-implements an owned capability instead of calling it; `record_geometry` at line 130 similarly re-derives the `(ring,)` wall tuple where the owner `scripts/prototypes/efit_field_swap/crosscheck.py:821 wall_units(record)` already builds it.

follow-on: the baseline_suite `command` carries the unsubstituted placeholder `<base-tree>` (`PYTHONPATH=<base-tree> ...`), so the recorded command is not the literal runnable command the delivery contract requires; the resolved path appears only in the log header of logs/gate-baseline-124302.log.

item_verdicts.done_when: the brief's three clauses are (1) both carriers as version-2 records read from the fixture store, (2) a README stating the boundary decision, (3) a committed round-trip test with one panel per record; all three are present (export_records.py, exports/README.md, test_export_records.py, docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/certified-carrier-export), and the round-trip gate measures clause 3, but the negative-control pointer that would evidence the gate's ability to fail is unusable at manifest.md:43.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to export one limited and one diverted nova certified analytic carrier as imas-efit version-2 boundary trace records; export_records.py:149 build_export and :252 write_export produce both records and docs/research/certified-carrier-export.html carries the decision table, so the goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, seven commits, a baseline of 2 collection errors at exit 2 and an after arm of 4 passed at exit 0, but `negative_control_log: NEG_LOG_PATH` at line 43 is a placeholder naming no file and the negative_control block claims a revision (055d84935) no complete red log covers.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source node was fenced to scripts/prototypes/certified_carrier_export, docs/research/certified-carrier-export.html, docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/certified-carrier-export.html and docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/certified-carrier-export plus run-dir logs and exports; all eight files in git diff 34d4c304b..055d84935 are inside those paths.

justifications.durability: test_export_records.py:71-72 asserts the re-read axis against the analytic certificate axis (an independent source) and :92-93 asserts the negated grid is refused with TopologyReason.NO_QUALIFIED_AXIS, both of which redden on a read regression, but :65-67 and :69 compare the re-read against record.axis_r/axis_z and record.fed_back_psi, which the producer stored from that same reading.
justifications.evidence: the after arm (4 passed, exit 0, logs/gate-after-125727.log with revision and EXIT lines) records the round trip and the baseline arm (exit 2) is recorded, but the declared negative_control_log is the placeholder NEG_LOG_PATH and the claimed revision 055d84935 has only truncated logs, so the gate's ability to fail is not citable.
justifications.fit: export_records.py follows the sibling prototype idiom with capability-named symbols and no plan label, but line 46 imports the private `_analytic_inputs` from the test module tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py into runtime code.
justifications.goal_fidelity: export_records.py:149 build_export builds and :252 write_export writes both carriers with the 65x65 analytic psi, the read axis, the polarity and the per-loop wall, and docs/research/certified-carrier-export.html states the limited/diverted decision and the certificate bounds.
justifications.reuse: the module correctly imports the codec owner's symbols (trace_record.py:40-44 TraceRecord, _closed_ring, write_trace_record) and reuses lattice, TraceSplineField, cached_carrier and certificate_field, but read_record (line 143) re-derives the convention that orientation.py:48 read_convention owns and record_geometry (line 130) re-derives the wall tuple that crosscheck.py:821 wall_units owns.
justifications.scope_discipline: every one of the eight files in git diff 34d4c304b..055d84935 (producer, gate.sh, test, panels, two docs, two SVGs) is inside the declared write paths and no out-of-scope path is touched.
